description: Eight gates weighed against each other and added into one voltage, in 8HP, with the weight of each bit under its own knob

params.text: Sets how much that bit adds to the total when it is high, 0 to 1; the eight come up as the binary weights, a hundred and twenty-eighth up to one
Sets how wide a span the output covers, 0V to 10V
Attenuates and inverts the range CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets where the span falls, -10V to +10V, read as its bottom, middle or top according to the button beside it
Attenuates and inverts the anchor CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Steps the anchor knob's meaning through minimum, centre and maximum, with a light showing which

inputs.text: Carries the eight bits as eight channels; a channel is a 1 at 1V or more and a 0 below that
The gate for that one bit, which overrides whatever the polyphonic input carries on that channel
Adds its voltage to the span after the trim knob
Adds its voltage to the anchor after the trim knob

outputs.text: Carries the weighted total of the eight bits, mapped into the chosen span
Carries the same total turned upside down within the span, so a high value here is a low one at the other output

notes: a bit with neither its own jack nor a channel of the polyphonic input reads 0, and all eight bits always count towards the total
with the weights left at their binary values the module matches a Turing Machine's Binary output exactly; changing the weights is what makes it a second voice from the same pattern
menu: Set weight-knobs 1-8 to: Binary (default), Binary reversed, Linear inc, Fixed/same, Random weights — sets all eight weight knobs at once
Quantize mode — rounds the output to the nearest step of the size chosen, from a twelfth of a volt up to 5V, and is Off unless you set it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
